public_rationale: The claim is that hallucinations had not gone away by late 2024, despite scaling and RAG. The evidence agrees. OpenAI's own Table 3 gives SimpleQA hallucination rates of 0.61 for GPT-4o and 0.44 for o1-preview, and OpenAI says more work is needed. A preregistered Stanford study found that RAG-based legal research tools from LexisNexis and Thomson Reuters hallucinated 17–33% of the time. In November 2024, ChatGPT Search (GPT-4o plus retrieval) got 153 of 200 source requests wrong or partly wrong. Rates fell in some cases, but none of these approaches removed the problem.
limitations: The benchmarks are hard by design, so the rates overstate typical everyday error rates.
The claim that the industry 'tried practically everything' is rhetoric and was not scored.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations in LLMs still have not gone away despite scaling and RAG.

statement.excerpt: Alas, even today hallucinations (probably better described as confabulations) still haven’t gone away. And not for lack of trying. The industry has tried practically everything, scaling, more scaling, and RAG.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post date, the leading LLMs, including scaled-up models and retrieval-augmented (RAG) systems, still produced hallucinations at noticeable rates.
'Even today' is an ongoing state. The target period is from the launch of GPT-4o (2024-05-13), ChatGPT's main model at the post date, to the post date itself.
'Tried practically everything' is rhetoric and is not scored.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that by late 2024 leading scaled or RAG-based systems had hallucination rates at or near zero on standard tests.
